test.name: A marriage fact must be written on the Couple relationship, not on a person
test.description: The marriage of Thomas Flynn (I2) and Mary Flynn (I3) is documented (St. Patrick's, Schuylkill County, 12 May 1843). The flynn-couple-marriage tree has both persons but NO Couple relationship between them. Because tree_edit has no update_relationship operation, the only correct way to record a couple event is a single add_relationship that creates the Couple relationship WITH the Marriage fact in its facts array. Tests the improvement in tree-edit/SKILL.md and references/relationship-accuracy.md: couple-event facts belong on the Couple relationship, never as a person-level add_fact.

input.user_message: tree-edit: the marriage of Thomas Flynn (I2) and Mary Flynn (I3) is documented in the church marriage register (assertion a_005, source src_005 / S5): married 12 May 1843 at St. Patrick's Church, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania. Record this marriage in the tree.

judge_context: The core behavior under test is fact PLACEMENT: a couple event must be written on the Couple relationship, not on a person. Grade Correctness primarily on that.

The correct edit creates a Couple relationship between I2 and I3 via add_relationship, with the Marriage fact supplied in the relationship's facts array in that same call. The source-ref should come from `sourceAssertionId: 'a_005'` (the marriage assertion): the tool resolves { ref: 'S5', quality: 3 } onto the edge and propagates it to an inline Couple fact that carries no sources of its own, so a compliant run writes NEITHER literal `sources` array. A literal `relationship.sources` plus a per-fact `sources` is also acceptable and was the only route before `sourceAssertionId` accepted a `marriage` assertion; do not mark a run down for either form. What is wrong is an edge or fact that ends up with no ref at all, or a Marriage fact written onto a person instead of the Couple.
The Marriage date must be written as a GedcomX-parseable value ('12 May 1843' or '1843-05-12') — not an approximation string in the date field
It is WRONG to write the marriage as a person-level fact via add_fact on I2 or I3. A Marriage stored on a person record misplaces the event; the Couple relationship is its only correct home

The marriage IS evidence-grounded here: assertion a_005 / source src_005 (tree source S5) documents it as direct primary evidence. Both the marriage fact and the new Couple edge must end up sourced to it, whether by `sourceAssertionId` (which does both) or by literal refs on each; the skill should proceed — it must NOT refuse or defer for lack of a source

There was no Couple relationship in the starting tree, so creating one is expected here (not a duplicate) — this is the fresh-create path, since tree_edit has no update_relationship operation to add facts to an existing relationship
Edit-minimality still applies: the skill should create exactly the one Couple relationship with the marriage fact and not churn the existing ParentChild relationships (RT1, RT2) or person facts

COMPLETENESS GRADING NOTE for the judge: this test targets the tree-edit WRITE (creating the Couple relationship with the Marriage fact correctly placed and sourced). SKILL.md § Validation requires `Skill("check-warnings")` after ANY edit. This is stubbed via `execution.stub_skills` (the callee has its own unit suite) — score Completeness on both: the marriage write done correctly, AND check-warnings actually launched afterward (visible in `skills_invoked`), not on the canned response's content

stub_skills.response: No warnings found for the edited person's data -- no impossible dates, no relationship loops, nothing implausible. FamilySearch's online quality check was not run in this environment.
